newsitem.title: USA: PSNH restores 345 MW Merrimack 2 coal unit.
newsitem.headline: PSNH restores 345 MW Merrimack 2 coal unit.

text.p: Public Service of New Hampshire (PSNH) said Thursday its coal-fired 345 megawatt (MW) Merrimack 2 power plant was back on line and running near full capacity, ending an unscheduled repair outage.
"The plant is back up near full load and operating normally. As of this morning we were at 308 MW," a PSNH spokesman said. "It began its restart Tuesday."
The unit was shut in late October for scheduled maintenance but failed an attempted restart November 22 due to problems with its generator rotor, prompting the extended outage.

The Merrimack facility is in Bow, central New Hampshire. Its other power plant, the 125 MW unit 1, is operating normally, the spokesman said. The two units account for about 23 percent of the utility's total electricity generation.
Public Service of New Hampshire is a subsidiary of Connecticut-based Northeast Utiltities.
